findings.where: All 12 screens (best on step 1 or step 9)
findings.what: The screens never write the size as |a|, never give the word magnitude, and never say a vector's letter is bold in print and underlined by hand. The brief promises this notation for lesson 1, and lesson 2 writes |v| cos θ, so add two short sentences such as 'We write its size |a|. Books call it the magnitude.' (in a steps lesson the explain text holding |a| = 5 is never shown).

'Arrow a runs 3 squares across and 4 up, at right angles, so Pythagoras gives its size: √(3² + 4²) = 5.' packs two ideas into one sentence, leaves 'at right angles' with nothing to attach to, and skips that the arrow's length is its size. Split it: 'Arrow a runs 3 squares across and 4 up. The two moves meet at a right angle, so Pythagoras gives its length: √(3² + 4²) = 5. That length is its size.' The read version needs the same change.

For the first 2.3 s of step 1 the grid is empty, and the readout shows across, up and size with no title or numbers until 3.2 s (step 5 until 2.6 s), so the opening frame shows no arrow to move and the readout looks broken. Fade the row labels in with their values, and start the arrow sooner or draw it faintly from the start.

The demonstration only stretches a from 1 to 2, so the shrink to a dot and the flip that the words describe appear only if Dan moves the slider himself. Let it sweep down through 0 to −1 and back up to 2, so it still ends on 2a and its read still matches.
The weight is the only thing drawn as an arrow before Check, so the picture gives away the answer. Put the weight on a tag like the other two and have the right answer draw its arrow.
The brief's 'parallel vectors are multiples of each other' never appears on screen. One sentence such as 'a, 2a and −2a lie along one line, so they are parallel' sets up collinearity for later.
To a sailor, 'It turns right round' can read as a turn to starboard. 'It reverses course at the same speed' says the same thing plainly.
'−v changes the sign of both parts' says 'parts', but every other screen says 'moves'. Keep 'moves' until components are named.

The first sentence has no verb, and 'The pump, the points and the boats are examples' talks about the lesson instead of to Dan. Try 'Each screen shows an arrow on a grid, with its moves and size beside it. The pump and boat figures are made up to keep the sums simple.'

findings.where: Step 7 slider label 'Number in front of a'
findings.what: The a here is plain text, but every other vector letter on the page is bold italic.

There are six footnote marks for five sources, and two sit mid-sentence ('negative,[^3] so', 'sizes.[^5]'). That is more than a few for one lesson. Keep the definition and the equal-vectors rule and drop the rest.

'Each line current has its own phase angle too' puts a phase angle (a shift in time) next to a direction in space before phasors are taught as different. Say that phase currents add by their angles in the same way, and leave the difference for the phasors lesson.
